notes.path: c4
notes.text: The English Opening starts with 1.c4. White controls the d5 square from the flank and meets 1...e5 with 2.Nc3.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3
notes.text: The King's English. With 1...e5, Black plays a Sicilian Defence with colours reversed, and White gets ready to fianchetto with g3.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3
notes.text: White prepares Bg2 to control d5 and the long light diagonal. If Black strikes with 3...d5, White swaps off the centre pawn with cxd5.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Bg2
notes.text: The bishop on g2 immediately hits the d5 knight and aims down the diagonal towards b7. After 5...Nb6, White develops Nf3.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3 Bb4
notes.text: Black pins the c3 knight to fight for e4. White simply finishes development with 4.Bg2.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 g3 Bb4 Bg2 O-O Nf3
notes.text: White develops the king's knight and attacks e5. If Black pushes 5...e4, the knight hops actively to d4.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3
notes.text: Black guards d5 and e5 with the knight. Against 3...g6, White puts the bishop on g2 and builds a flexible queenside attack.

notes.path: c4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 d3 d6
notes.text: With d3 holding e4 and the g2 bishop unblocked, White develops 6.Nf3 and prepares O-O, Rb1 and b4.

notes.path: c4 c5
notes.text: The Symmetrical Variation. White plays 2.Nc3 to control d5 before choosing where the pawns go.

notes.path: c4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7
notes.text: Both sides mirror each other on the long diagonal. White develops 5.Nf3 and stays ready to castle and play d3 or d4.

notes.path: c4 c5 Nc3 Nf6 g3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 Bg2
notes.text: Black takes space in the centre early. After 5...Nc7, White plays Nf3 and castles before expanding on the queenside.

notes.path: c4 Nf6
notes.text: Against 1...Nf6, White develops 2.Nc3 to fight for d5 and keep the option of g3 or Nf3.

notes.path: c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 g3 Bg7 Bg2
notes.text: Against Black's King's Indian set-up, White develops calmly with Nf3 and castles short.

notes.path: c4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 g3
notes.text: White trades off Black's d-pawn and fianchettoes the bishop. If Black takes on c3, White recaptures bxc3 to strengthen the centre.

notes.path: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6
notes.text: Black prepares ...d5 or ...Bb4. White develops 3.Nf3 so the knight on c3 cannot be pinned cleanly after ...d5.

notes.path: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3 Bb4
notes.text: Black pins the c3 knight like a Nimzo-Indian. White plays 4.Qc2 to protect c3 and avoid doubled pawns.

notes.path: c4 e6
notes.text: Against 1...e6, White plays 2.Nf3 first to stay in Catalan and English waters without committing d4 early.

notes.path: c4 e6 Nf3 d5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 Be7 O-O O-O
notes.text: Both kings are safe. Now 6.d4 opens a favourable Catalan where the g2 bishop pressures Black's queenside.

notes.path: c4 c6
notes.text: Black prepares a Slav-style pawn wall with ...d5. White develops 2.Nf3 and fianchettoes with g3 and Bg2.

notes.path: c4 c6 Nf3 d5 g3 Nf6 Bg2 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5
notes.text: Black has left the b7 pawn behind. White plays 6.Qb3 to attack both b7 and d5 at once.

notes.path: c4 d5
notes.text: Black challenges c4 at once without support. White trades 2.cxd5 so Black must lose time with the queen or knight.

notes.path: c4 d5 cxd5 Qxd5 Nc3
notes.text: White develops with tempo against Black's queen. After 3...Qa5, White continues with Nf3 and g3.
